source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities

coverage.scope: C. Unsecured Distributions §726 and plan confirmations for Chapters 11,12,13/Subchapter V; D.1 §507 priority sequence and superpriorities
coverage.note: Textbook indexing amounts are from 2021 edition and NOT represented as 2026 limits.

topics.title: C.1 — Chapter 7 Unsecured Distributions: Six §726 Tiers
topics.description: Secured and exempt property first; strict rank ordering, pro rata within tier and no-asset cases.

entries.title: §725 secured collateral and §522 exemptions precede unsecured pool
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Secured creditors receive collateral/value under enforceable liens; individual's exemptions remove protected estate interests; remaining net estate then follows §726 for unsecured creditors.
entries.laymanExplanation: Not every estate asset becomes cash for credit card bills: first account for liens and exemptions.
entries.legalExplanation: Casebook example assets $20k, lien obligations $12k, residual $8k fully exempt → zero general unsecured distribution.
entries.examApplication: For hypothetical subtract secured recovery, then exemptions, then administrative costs and distribution tiers.
entries.examTrap: Having property doesn't mean a Chapter 7 case has funds for general unsecured creditors.

entries.title: No-asset Chapter 7 means no general unsecured distribution
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Casebook says over 90% Chapter 7 filings were no-asset at source time; secured assets/exemptions/administration may consume remainder.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor may own house, clothes and car yet trustee has nothing distributable after liens/protection.
entries.legalExplanation: This is descriptive historical source statistic, not current statistical verification.
entries.examApplication: In essay distinguish total assets, nonexempt equity, total secured loans and estate net value.
entries.examTrap: 'No asset' doesn't mean debtor owns literally nothing.

entries.title: Strict §726 ordering, full tier before next; §726(b) pro rata
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Every allowed claim within higher tier must be satisfied before next tier receives anything; insufficient funds within tier divided pro rata by claim size.
entries.laymanExplanation: If money runs out while paying priority wages, normal credit card creditors get zero.
entries.legalExplanation: Section §726(b) pro rata within class of equal rank; courts may not invent different distribution sequence.
entries.examApplication: To distribute $10k over $20k equal-tier claims: recovery percentage =10/20=50%; $4k claim gets $2k.
entries.examTrap: Do not allocate dollars to lower tier before fully satisfying higher.

entries.title: Tier 1 — §726(a)(1) priority claims under §507
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Priority unsecured claims §507 paid first within §726; ten priority ranks are themselves ordinal and must be paid from highest to lowest.
entries.laymanExplanation: Child support may get ahead of administrative costs and normal lenders per ranked statutory list.
entries.legalExplanation: Priority claims still unsecured unless also backed by lien; see D priority matrix.
entries.examApplication: Identify rank and compare competing priorities.
entries.examTrap: 'Priority' isn't synonym for secured.

entries.title: Tier 2 — §726(a)(2) timely nonpriority unsecured + certain unnotified late
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Allowed nonpriority unsecured claims with timely proofs, and certain late proofs filed without notice soon enough to share payout, receive second level.
entries.laymanExplanation: Ordinary credit card, medical bill, contract claim can share after priority claims fully covered.
entries.legalExplanation: Exception in §726(a)(2)(C) requires BOTH lack of notice and filing in time to permit distribution.
entries.examApplication: In problem about late proof ask notice and filing timing.
entries.examTrap: Don't include every late proof in second tier.

entries.title: Tier 3 — §726(a)(3) other tardy unsecured claims
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Ordinary nonpriority proofs filed late without qualifying absence-of-notice exception paid only after full second-tier payment.
entries.laymanExplanation: Late creditor may still get money—but behind on-time creditors.
entries.legalExplanation: Track bar date and whether second-tier pool fully paid.
entries.examApplication: If estate has surplus beyond timely claims, consider tier 3.
entries.examTrap: Not all late claims are necessarily completely void.

entries.title: Tier 4 — §726(a)(4) noncompensatory penalties
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Fines/penalties/forfeitures not compensating pecuniary harm are subordinated after ordinary compensatory unsecured claims.
entries.laymanExplanation: Punishment claims usually don't take creditors' limited compensation first.
entries.legalExplanation: Book distinguishes penalty treatment at §726 from §507(a)(8) tax priority and administrative penalties analysis.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish fine for punishment vs compensatory victim damages.
entries.examTrap: Don't blindly classify any environmental monetary obligation as tier 4.

entries.title: Tier 5 — §726(a)(5) postpetition interest in solvent estate
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: When tiers 1–4 fully paid, unsecured creditors may receive interest on allowed claims at legal rate before debtor receives surplus.
entries.laymanExplanation: If estate pays all creditors in full, then add legal interest before returning extra to debtor.
entries.legalExplanation: This is separate from normal §502(b)(2) disallowance of unmatured interest and from oversecured §506(b).
entries.examApplication: Compute allowed debts first, then check solvent surplus for legal interest.
entries.examTrap: Don't pay tier 5 interest before even one unpaid tier 2 claim.

entries.title: Tier 6 — §726(a)(6) residual to debtor
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Any estate money after satisfying all creditors and interest as statutory scheme demands goes back to debtor.
entries.laymanExplanation: If every creditor and interest is paid, owner gets leftovers.
entries.legalExplanation: Secured rights and exemptions already separately addressed.
entries.examApplication: Only conclude debtor recovers surplus after first five tiers complete.
entries.examTrap: Filing doesn't automatically forfeit all property value if estate solvent.

entries.title: Numeric distribution example (two second-tier claims)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: If priority tier paid and $10k remains for $20k allowed ordinary unsecured: percentage $10k÷$20k=0.50; claimant A allowed $8k receives $4k; claimant B allowed $12k receives $6k.
entries.laymanExplanation: A 50-cent-on-the-dollar payout is equal by percentage, not equal dollar checks.
entries.legalExplanation: Formula each claim payout = remaining tier fund×individual allowed claim÷total allowed claims of that tier.
entries.examApplication: Use to compute any §726(b) shortfall.
entries.examTrap: Never give both claims same $5k if their allowed debts unequal.

topics.title: C.2 — Chapter 11, Subchapter V, Chapter 12 and 13 Payment Plans
topics.description: Plan voting, classification, liquidation floor, priority payment, cramdown and disposable income.

entries.title: Chapter 11/12/13 usually distribute future earnings under confirmed plan
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Unlike one-time Chapter 7 liquidation, reorganizing debtors pay creditors over time from future income/business operations; plan confirmation controls timing/classification and statutory protections.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor keeps earning and pays over years rather than selling everything on day one.
entries.legalExplanation: Plan treatment subject best-interests liquidation floor and priorities; differences by chapter.
entries.examApplication: Identify debtor and chapter before applying creditor voting rules.
entries.examTrap: Chapter 12 and 13 are not miniature Chapter 11 votes.

entries.title: §507 priority generally full payment required in plans
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Chapter 11 §1129(a)(9), Chapter 12 §1222(a)(2), Chapter 13 §1322(a)(2) generally require full priority claim payment through plan unless holder agrees or statutory variations.
entries.laymanExplanation: Plans usually must make priority support and tax creditors whole even if ordinary unsecured creditors receive pennies.
entries.legalExplanation: Different treatment/timing of priority categories permitted subject chapter-specific rules.
entries.examApplication: First classify priority vs general unsecured, then draft plan recovery.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume every priority claim can be reduced by debtor just because creditors vote.

entries.title: Chapter 11 classes: §§1122,1123 and §1126 voting
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Only substantially similar claims in a class; plan gives same treatment within class. Classes vote after court-approved disclosure under §1125; accepting class binds individual dissenters subject statutory protection.
entries.laymanExplanation: Group similar creditors, then let class vote; dissenter can be bound by majority if floor satisfied.
entries.legalExplanation: Class voting applies to Chapter 11 and necessary plan acceptance tests; cramdown if class rejects.
entries.examApplication: If $100k and $5k same-class creditors disagree, examine acceptance at class level.
entries.examTrap: No general class votes for Chapter 12 or Chapter 13 unsecured claimants.

entries.title: Chapter 11 best-interests §1129(a)(7) protects individual dissenters
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Even class acceptance cannot force a creditor who votes no to take less in plan than it would get under hypothetical Chapter 7 liquidation at effective date.
entries.laymanExplanation: Plan must offer at least what creditor would get if company liquidated today.
entries.legalExplanation: Best-interest is individual liquidation comparison; separate from cramdown fair/equitable class treatment.
entries.examApplication: Compute expected Chapter 7 payout for objector and compare present value of plan distribution.
entries.examTrap: Don't think class vote overrides individual's Chapter 7 minimum.

entries.title: Rejecting Chapter 11 class: §1129(b) unfair discrimination and fair/equitable
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Cramdown over dissenting class requires no unfair discrimination and fair/equitable treatment; class rank/priority and possible full payment are key.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor can sometimes confirm without class consent but must follow tougher fairness rules.
entries.legalExplanation: Textbook describes senior not >100%, equally ranked classes not unfairly favored, junior nothing unless dissenting unsecured fully paid.
entries.examApplication: Identify senior/equal/junior classes and amounts before applying absolute priority.
entries.examTrap: No general exemption for ordinary corporate Chapter 11 from absolute priority.

entries.title: Absolute priority rule §1129(b)(2)(B)(ii)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Absent exception, holders junior to a dissenting unsecured class cannot receive or retain property under plan on account of junior interest unless dissenting class fully paid.
entries.laymanExplanation: Owners normally can't keep company shares while rejecting unsecured creditors receive a haircut.
entries.legalExplanation: Analyze whether shareholder equity retains value on account of old interest; separate consensual plan or special subchapter laws.
entries.examApplication: If general unsecured class rejects 20% plan while old equity retains shares, flag absolute priority.
entries.examTrap: Do not apply same absolute priority rule to Subchapter V nonconsensual confirmation.

entries.title: Individual Chapter 11 §1129(a)(15) disposable income protection
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: When eligible unsecured creditor objects in individual Chapter 11, plan must generally devote at least five years of projected disposable income (or equivalent value) to creditor payments.
entries.laymanExplanation: Individual debtor can't retain high future disposable income while offering nothing if creditor objects.
entries.legalExplanation: Section 1129(a)(15) plan-specific statutory protection, alongside other confirmation requirements.
entries.examApplication: Identify natural-person Chapter 11 and objection, compare §1325(b) chapter 13.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply individual-Ch11 rule wholesale to business corporation.

entries.title: Subchapter V §1191(b),(c): disposable income instead of absolute priority
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: In nonconsensual small-business Subchapter V Chapter 11, §1191 permits confirmation with defined fair/equitable projected disposable income devotion for 3–5 years instead of ordinary absolute priority rule.
entries.laymanExplanation: Small business owner may retain ownership while paying sustainable plan income for set period.
entries.legalExplanation: Subchapter V status requires eligibility not described in Chapter 5; source focuses on payment mechanism.
entries.examApplication: Check this is actually Subchapter V before relaxing rule.
entries.examTrap: Don't say owner retention is always free and without payment obligations.

entries.title: Chapters 12/13: no unsecured creditor class vote; objections available
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Debtor proposes plan confirmed if §§1225/1325 met; unsecured creditors object but do not vote. Claims in same class receive same treatment and classifications cannot unfairly discriminate.
entries.laymanExplanation: Creditors in personal plan can object to unfair treatment but don't cast ballots for plan.
entries.legalExplanation: §§1222(a)(3),(b)(1),1322(a)(3),(b)(1) govern equal treatment/nonunfair discrimination.
entries.examApplication: Discuss class treatment and best-interests rather than nonexistent voting mechanism.
entries.examTrap: Do not claim Chapter 13 plan rejected because majority unsecured creditors vote no.

entries.title: Best-interests floor in Chapters 12 & 13
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: §§1225(a)(4),1325(a)(4) require unsecured creditors at least what Chapter 7 hypothetical liquidation would provide.
entries.laymanExplanation: If debtor could liquidate assets and pay $5k, plan cannot give relevant unsecured creditors less than that floor.
entries.legalExplanation: Liquidation test may require zero when debtor has no nonexempt equity; projected disposable income is separate rule.
entries.examApplication: Compute lien/exemption net equity and pro rata unsecured payout as baseline.
entries.examTrap: Zero liquidation floor doesn't imply zero payment plan if debtor has excess income.

entries.title: Projected disposable income commitment in Chapters 12 & 13
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Upon trustee/unsecured creditor objection, debtor generally devotes projected disposable income for applicable period; Chapter 13 above median typically 5 years, below median typically 3 years (subject Code).
entries.laymanExplanation: Even debtor with no property may need to pay from tomorrow's paychecks.
entries.legalExplanation: Chapter 5 ties back to Chapter 2 means testing and Lanning future income approach.
entries.examApplication: Apply both best-interests and disposable-income tests—they are independent obligations.
entries.examTrap: Don't use assets-only analysis to approve zero plan for well-paid debtor.

topics.title: D.1 — The Ten Statutory §507(a) Priority Ranks
topics.description: Mandatory ranking, narrow construction, source-era dollar caps and superpriorities.

entries.title: Priorities are statutory, strictly construed and ordinal
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: §507(a) ranks ten unsecured priority categories by number; priority claimant bears proof; higher class paid in full before lower, and same rank shares pro rata. States/courts cannot invent their own bankruptcy priority.
entries.laymanExplanation: Like numbered boarding groups: first class fully paid before next; those in same group split remaining by claim size.
entries.legalExplanation: §726(b) equality within rank and Supremacy Clause preemption of state priorities; §545(1) avoids insolvency-only statutory liens.
entries.examApplication: For multiple claims label each §507(a) rank, never just 'special'.
entries.examTrap: Equity alone doesn't elevate sympathetic creditor into statutory priority.

entries.title: Priority 1 — domestic support §507(a)(1)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Prepetition domestic support owed to eligible spouse/former spouse/child/guardian or assigned government receives highest general §507 priority; subranking favors direct family claim.
entries.laymanExplanation: Overdue child support is at top of unsecured priority queue.
entries.legalExplanation: Debtor may also face nondischargeability §523(a)(5) and other special collection rules.
entries.examApplication: For 5.3(b) put support $20k ahead of estate expenses/tax in statutory rank, then consider admin exceptions and exact amounts.
entries.examTrap: Don't presume the 1st rank means support is secured.

entries.title: Priority 2 — administrative expenses and court fees §507(a)(2)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: §503(b) actual necessary estate operating/administration claims and specified title 28 court charges enjoy second priority; exceptions include sub-superpriorities.
entries.laymanExplanation: Work done to run bankruptcy is paid before most old loans.
entries.legalExplanation: Postpetition transaction/benefit general test and Reading exceptions detailed separately.
entries.examApplication: Determine which work/postpetition cost vs old debt.
entries.examTrap: Not every expense incurred after filing is automatically admin.

entries.title: Priority 3 — involuntary filing gap claims
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: §507(a)(3) and §502(f): qualifying unsecured credit incurred during interval between involuntary petition and entry of relief order.
entries.laymanExplanation: Businesses can continue during contested petition; new gap suppliers get special protection.
entries.legalExplanation: Recall Chapter 2 §303(f) gap and §502(f) characterization.
entries.examApplication: Mark date of involuntary petition and order; divide services across boundary.
entries.examTrap: Does not include every old debt simply due during gap.

entries.title: Priority 4 — employee wages §507(a)(4)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Eligible wages/commissions etc earned in 180-day period before petition or business closing (whichever earlier) up to printed book cap $13,650 per person (2021 source-era indexed figure).
entries.laymanExplanation: Worker last paychecks get extra protection but capped.
entries.legalExplanation: Priority based on performance timing, not payment/vesting; current indexed amount may differ.
entries.examApplication: For vacation/pay problem accrue by service period and isolate eligible prepetition share.
entries.examTrap: Don't use 2021 dollar cap as verified 2026 law.

entries.title: Priority 5 — unpaid employee benefit plan contributions §507(a)(5)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Eligible contributions from services during 180 days before earlier of petition or business shutdown, subject aggregate/coordinate cap with rank-4 wages.
entries.laymanExplanation: Missed employer pension/health contributions get rank after wages.
entries.legalExplanation: Amount cap interacts with employee wage maximum.
entries.examApplication: Compute wage priority used and remaining available benefit limit.
entries.examTrap: Not unlimited in addition to wage priority.

entries.title: Priority 6 — grain producers / U.S. fishermen §507(a)(6)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Producer claims against grain storage and U.S. fishermen against fish storage/processing debtors protected up to printed book cap $6,725 each (historical indexed).
entries.laymanExplanation: Farmers and fishing suppliers have special statutory protection from storage company insolvency.
entries.legalExplanation: Book recounts farmer uprising motivating 1984 enactment.
entries.examApplication: Check correct type of business and producer claimant.
entries.examTrap: Ordinary grocery distributor claim doesn't become rank6 just because food involved.

entries.title: Priority 7 — personal layaway deposits §507(a)(7)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Individual consumer prepetition deposit for personal/family/household undelivered goods or services protected to printed book cap $3,025 each (historical indexed).
entries.laymanExplanation: Prepaid but never received personal-training sessions may qualify.
entries.legalExplanation: Need consumer individual, money paid, undelivered promised personal use, statutory max.
entries.examApplication: For 5.3(c) separate training received from unprovided value.
entries.examTrap: A business purchasing inventory isn't a consumer layaway claimant.

entries.title: Priority 8 — qualifying prepetition taxes §507(a)(8)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Specified income/property/withholding/employment/excise/customs/tax-related penalty claims receive eighth priority if temporal/form requirements met; postpetition estate taxes instead administrative expenses.
entries.laymanExplanation: Tax authority's old tax bill ranks below many other categories, but can survive discharge for individual.
entries.legalExplanation: Income tax three-year due/240-day assessment/assessable-after tests detailed later.
entries.examApplication: For 5.3(b) test 2016 tax return due in 2017 vs March1 2020 filing; timing critical.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume all old taxes priority forever.

entries.title: Priority 9 — bank depository capital commitments §507(a)(9)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Specified commitments to maintain capital of insured depository institutions given ninth priority.
entries.laymanExplanation: Narrow banking stabilization-related claims have special rank.
entries.legalExplanation: Exam likely limited recognition; statutory §507 governs.
entries.examApplication: Identify relevant institution/commitment rather than generic bank debt.
entries.examTrap: Not every bank account claim qualifies.

entries.title: Priority 10 — DUI death/personal injury §507(a)(10)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Claims for death/personal injury from unlawful intoxicated operation of motor vehicle/vessel receive tenth priority, with related discharge exception §523(a)(9).
entries.laymanExplanation: DUI injury victim special priority below nine earlier ranks, but above ordinary unsecured.
entries.legalExplanation: Separate from general tort claim due solely to negligent driving.
entries.examApplication: Check intoxication and resulting death/personal injury.
entries.examTrap: No priority for every traffic ticket or property-only collision.

entries.title: §507(b) and §364(c)(1) superpriority overrides
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: If secured creditor's granted adequate protection proves insufficient, §507(b) superpriority over other admin. Postpetition estate lender may receive §364(c)(1) priority over admin to induce financing.
entries.laymanExplanation: Some special postfiling creditors move ahead even of normal administration claims.
entries.legalExplanation: Must prove failed protection under secured use or court-approved debtor-in-possession financing.
entries.examApplication: Before distributing, test liens and special superpriority ahead of §507 list.
entries.examTrap: Don't create superpriority without statutory predicate or order.

entries.title: De facto priority through required estate compliance
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §§C, D.1: Chapter 7 and reorganization unsecured distributions, §507 priorities
entries.summary: Certain ongoing obligations (e.g. postpetition collective bargaining, environmental cleanup) may be paid during case before distributions even if not formally §507 priority.
entries.laymanExplanation: Being ordered to actually comply can make someone effectively paid first.
entries.legalExplanation: Compare Penn Terra, Midlantic, Apex and Reading but distinguish legal statutory ranking from compelled current action.
entries.examApplication: Explain real-world economic effect separately from formal priority.
entries.examTrap: A de facto economic preference doesn't automatically mean bankruptcy court awarded §507 claim priority.
